newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PARLIAMENT BODY BACKS CHEAP FARMS FUEL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PARLIAMENT BODY BACKS CHEAP FARMS FUEL.

text.p: The Polish parliament's committees on Tuesday cleared a controversial bill on providing subsidised diesel fuel for farmers, which will cost the budget about 600 million zlotys, PAP news agency said.
Under the bill, which will now go for a second reading in the lower house, the farming diesel will be exempted from the excise tax during the next four years.
The cheap fuel would be coloured and its use for non-agricultural purposes would be prohibited.
Under an alternative proposal, farmers would be entitled to refunds of the excise tax levied on the diesel fuel.

The bill has been heavily criticed by Grzegorz Kolodko, who on Tuesday quit the post of the finance minister, saying he did not want to get involved in the compaign to this year's parliamentary elections.
Kolodko had said the draft, which would cost taxpayers about 600 million, would unfairly privilege farmers over other social groups.

The Polish Peasant Party (PSL), the smaller group in the ruling leftsit coalition, put forward the bill, saying it would make agricultural production more profitable and help in the sector's restructuring.
Some analysts have said the bill, if approved, will boost the PSL's chances in the elections, due after August, this year. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
